narrative:
The model determined that you have a 43% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability crossed the threshold the bank uses, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that weighed most heavily in this decision were the length of the loan you requested, the status of your checking account, and the total amount you wanted to borrow. Your relatively short 10-month repayment period actually worked in your favor and pulled the prediction toward approval. However, this positive effect was outweighed by two other important elements. Having a checking account that shows between 0 and 200 DM is fairly common among applicants, yet the model viewed this particular balance as a signal of higher risk, pushing the outcome toward denial. The loan amount of 1,521 DM was lower than the average requested by approved applicants, which again helped your case, but not enough to overcome the concerns raised by your account status.

Taken together, these factors led the bank to decide against approving the loan. You may wish to reapply after improving your checking account balance or consider requesting a longer repayment period, which the model treats more favorably. Reviewing your overall financial picture with a loan officer could also reveal additional steps that would strengthen a future application.
